name: Primary mediastinal B-cell lymphoma
theme: the young-mediastinal entity · the radiation-sparing turn

meta.title: PMBCL in silico decision trainer
meta.condition: Primary mediastinal B-cell lymphoma, adult and AYA
meta.population: Patients with PMBCL - THE BETWEEN-TWO-TRAINERS ENTITY: a thymic B-cell lymphoma of young adults (female-predominant, median age ~30s - review-sourced) sitting biologically between the dlbcl and hodgkin trainers, sharing 9p24.1 PD-L1/PD-L2 amplification with nodular-sclerosing Hodgkin (verified receipt) while wearing a DLBCL-adjacent face. Rare (~2-4% of NHL, review-sourced), bulky-anterior-mediastinal by signature, and capable of presenting as an EMERGENCY (SVC syndrome - the supportive honesty). The era's headline is THE RADIATION-SPARING TURN: two different roads now reach no-radiation in most patients, and the randomized receipt for omission exists. The confusables guard the door: DLBCL-NOS reroutes LIVE to the dlbcl trainer (the registry's fifth live reroute) and mediastinal gray-zone lymphoma - the true between-entity - carries its own honest thinness.
meta.summary: Evidence-linked teaching application for the young-mediastinal entity, built around THE TWO ROADS TO NO RADIATION: (1) DA-EPOCH-R (the NCI receipt: 93% EFS / 97% OS with NO mediastinal radiotherapy in 51 patients - THE SOFT-FLAGGED FLAGSHIP: its NEJM PMID is snippet-bound only this sweep, said on the card; the 156-patient multicenter confirmation matched) and (2) R-CHOP with the EOT-PET-guided radiation decision - now carrying the RANDOMIZED omission receipt: IELSG-37 (verified) randomized complete-metabolic-responders to observation vs 30 Gy and observation was NON-INFERIOR (30-month PFS 96.…
meta.disclaimer: Synthetic teaching environment. Not medical advice; every number is a claim with a citation and an expiry date.
meta.classification: WHO5 + ICC 2022 (both verified; PMBCL stable as a distinct entity; the ICC citation-entry and WHO5 Correction-entry traps caught again); mediastinal gray-zone lymphoma as its own entity in both (restricted to mediastinal EBV-negative cases); the DLBCL-NOS distinction ultimately by gene expression (the founding Rosenwald/Savage PMIDs unverified this sweep - flagged)
meta.response: THE EOT-PET ROUTER (IELSG-26, verified): mediastinal residual masses persist WITHOUT disease - the Deauville read (liver cutpoint) decides, not the CT mass: 5-yr PFS 99% (DS 1-3) vs 68% (DS 4-5). End-of-treatment PET is this disease's single most decision-loaded artifact

Patient.label: Age
Patient.help: A disease of young adults (median ~30s, female-predominant - review-sourced): cure is the expectation and late effects are the long game.
Patient.helpPatient: Most patients are young adults - the plan protects the decades ahead as deliberately as it treats the disease.

Patient.label: Performance status (ECOG)
Patient.help: Often driven by the mass itself (compression, effusions) - and improves fast once treatment starts.
Patient.helpPatient: Feeling unwell here is usually the mass pressing on things - it typically improves quickly with treatment.

Disease.label: Entity confirmation (the three-way read)
Disease.help: The three-way read: DLBCL-NOS reroutes LIVE to the dlbcl trainer (the registry's fifth live reroute); mediastinal GRAY-ZONE lymphoma - the true between-entity, its own diagnosis in both 2022 classifi…
Disease.helpPatient: Three look-alike lymphomas live in this location - an expert review of a good-sized biopsy tells them apart, and the treatments differ.

Disease.label: Staging workup
Disease.help: PET/CT staging plus the fertility-preservation referral BEFORE cycle one - the young population's clock is part of the workup.
Disease.helpPatient: The scans map the disease - and for young patients, fertility preservation is discussed before treatment starts, not after.

Presentation.label: SVC syndrome / airway compression
Presentation.help: A substantial minority present with SVC syndrome (review-sourced, wide range - flagged): the craft is adequate tissue FAST (steroids-before-biopsy degrade the specimen) and urgent treatment start - t…
Presentation.helpPatient: Sometimes the mass presses on the big vein or airway and treatment must start urgently - the team gets the biopsy quickly first, because the diagnosis steers everything.

R/R routing.label: Prior CAR-T
R/R routing.help: Post-CAR-T patients have a randomized option at the highest-risk moment: SWOG S2114 (consolidation vs observation - PMBCL named, mosunetuzumab in reach).
R/R routing.helpPatient: For patients who have already had cell therapy, a study asks whether adding consolidation treatment right after helps.

Newly diagnosed.name: DA-EPOCH-R (road one: intensify, skip radiation up front)
Newly diagnosed.guideline: a frontline standard (NCCN secondhand) - the radiation-sparing-by-intensification road
Newly diagnosed.evidence: phase 2 NCI + multicenter confirmation (flagship PMID soft-flagged, said); the tie is the cross-trial honesty
Newly diagnosed.toxicity: infusional intensity - cytopenias, lines, admissions for some; bought against no radiation to a young chest
Newly diagnosed.patient: Road one: a more intensive chemotherapy-antibody program designed so that radiation is not needed at all - the road that first proved most patients cure without it.

Newly diagnosed.name: R-CHOP + the PET-guided radiation decision (road two: the randomized omission receipt)
Newly diagnosed.guideline: a frontline standard (NCCN secondhand) - the radiation-sparing-by-PET road (IELSG-37 verified)
Newly diagnosed.evidence: randomized omission receipt (verified) on this road's PET question; the tie is the cross-trial honesty
Newly diagnosed.toxicity: standard R-CHOP ledger - gentler delivery; the road's radiation exposure now falls only on the PET-positive minority
Newly diagnosed.patient: Road two: standard outpatient chemotherapy-antibody cycles, with the radiation question answered by the end-of-treatment scan - and a randomized trial has now proven that a fully clean scan safely means NO radiation.

Newly diagnosed.name: Consolidative RT (the PET-positive minority's road)
Newly diagnosed.guideline: the PET-positive pathway (IELSG-37 protocol convention; NCCN secondhand)
Newly diagnosed.evidence: cohort-verified floor (IELSG-26) with protocol-grade pathway; flagged composite figure
Newly diagnosed.toxicity: mediastinal RT in a young chest - exactly the cost the two roads exist to avoid, spent only where the PET insists
Newly diagnosed.patient: For the minority whose end-of-treatment scan stays truly positive: focused radiation - the tool held in reserve for exactly this reading, after the reading is double-checked.

Newly diagnosed.name: Comfort-focused care
Newly diagnosed.guideline: always on the menu, never by drift
Newly diagnosed.patient: Declining treatment is a real choice - named honestly in a disease where cure is the strong expectation.

Relapsed / recurrent.name: CD19 CAR-T (the label names this disease - and it answers)
Relapsed / recurrent.guideline: label-inclusive (PMBCL named) - the R/R spine by receipt and biology
Relapsed / recurrent.evidence: ZUMA-1 verified (all-LBCL figures flagged as such); PMBCL-better signal at flagged-PMID grade
Relapsed / recurrent.toxicity: CRS/ICANS window at certified centers - a young population tolerates the ride comparatively well
Relapsed / recurrent.patient: The engineered-cell therapy - approved by name for this disease, and the real-world evidence suggests it works even better here than in its more common cousin.

Relapsed / recurrent.name: Checkpoint blockade (the 9p24 payoff - both analyses taught)
Relapsed / recurrent.guideline: accelerated approval 2018 (secondhand; conversion status UNRESOLVED - flagged)
Relapsed / recurrent.evidence: phase 2 (both analyses verified) - ORR-labeled: displays, never ranks; the tail said
Relapsed / recurrent.toxicity: the immune ledger - gentle enough to bridge, real enough to watch
Relapsed / recurrent.patient: Immunotherapy that works here because of this disease's specific biology - shared with Hodgkin lymphoma: most benefit goes to those who reach a complete response, where it tends to last.

Relapsed / recurrent.name: Chemo-salvage then ASCT (the chemosensitive minority's road - the receipt says minority)
Relapsed / recurrent.guideline: the legacy road, honestly demoted (NCCN secondhand) - for the chemosensitive minority
Relapsed / recurrent.evidence: the worse-than-analog receipt verified; the conditional ASCT promise verified; floor flagged
Relapsed / recurrent.toxicity: salvage-intensity chemotherapy + transplant - spent only where the response fork earns it
Relapsed / recurrent.patient: The older path - strong chemotherapy then a stem-cell transplant - now honestly reserved for the minority whose disease still answers chemotherapy, because this disease answers it less often than its cousins.

Relapsed / recurrent.name: Comfort-focused care
Relapsed / recurrent.guideline: always on the menu, never by drift
Relapsed / recurrent.patient: Comfort-focused care remains a real choice at every step.

milestones.title: Distinguish PMBCL from cHL/grey-zone
review: PMBCL vs nodular-sclerosis cHL vs GREY-ZONE - three mediastinal diseases; grey-zone does WORSE than either parent (EFS 62%/OS 74% firsthand) and must not be shoehorned
regimen picks the radiation question: DA-EPOCH-R was built to omit RT (5-yr EFS 93% no-RT); R-CHOP-family answers with the PET (IELSG37: observation noninferior in CMR)
the PET is read at the LIVER cutoff (IELSG26: 99-vs-68 5-yr PFS) - blood-pool strictness over-irradiates
9p24.1 biology licenses the checkpoint door at relapse - and its durability is bimodal (KN-170: DoR not reached in CRs, PFS 4.3 overall)

Dunleavy et al. DA-EPOCH-R in PMBCL (NEJM 2013;368:1408-16): n=51 NCI - 5-yr EFS 93%, OS 97%, ZERO mediastinal radiotherapy. THE SOFT-FLAGGED FLAGSHIP: PMID 23574119 is SNIPPET-BOUND only this sweep (WebFetch denied; two independent snippets bound it to the exact title - and the near-title REVIEW at 23863060 was caught masquerading as it). Direct PubMed re-check before ship. The hypothesized 'CALGB 51,301' PMBCL trial DOES NOT EXIST (trap caught - dropped) | PMID 23574119 + abstract read firsthand 2026-08-26

Giulino-Roth et al. multicenter DA-EPOCH-R confirmation (PMID 29082519, pubmed-url-match): n=156 adults + children (3-yr EFS ~86%, OS ~95% - memory grade); comparative real-world DA-EPOCH-R vs R-CHOP (31606909, matched; numbers not pulled) | PMID 29082519 + abstract read firsthand 2026-08-26

IELSG-37 (PMID 39159403, pubmed-url-match; JCO 2024): 545 enrolled, 268 CMR patients RANDOMIZED - observation (n=132) vs 30 Gy (n=136): 30-month PFS 96.2% vs 98.5% (HR 1.47, CI 0.34-6.28); 5-yr OS 99% BOTH arms - observation NON-INFERIOR: THE RANDOMIZED RADIATION-OMISSION RECEIPT. Companion regimen-impact paper (40939190, matched). The pre-rituximab-era RT RCT (22172907, matched) is the legacy contrast | PMID 39159403 + abstract read firsthand 2026-08-26

IELSG-26 (PMID 24799481, pubmed-url-match; JCO 2014 - the ADJACENT-PMID trap at 24799491 caught): EOT-PET by Deauville liver cutpoint - 5-yr PFS 99% (DS 1-3) vs 68% (DS 4-5); OS 100% vs 83%. THE ROUTER RECEIPT: residual masses persist without disease. NCI serial-PET companion (29895624 + letter 30065020, matched); IELSG-37 PET segmentation follow-on (39819690, matched) | PMID 24799481 + abstract read firsthand 2026-08-26

Green et al. (Blood 2010;116:3268-77, PMID 20628145, pubmed-url-match): selective 9p24.1 amplification with PD-L1/PD-L2 expression + JAK2 induction in NS-Hodgkin AND PMBCL - THE HODGKIN-ADJACENCY RECEIPT: the biology that earned the checkpoint chapter | PMID 20628145 + abstract read firsthand 2026-08-26

KEYNOTE-170, BOTH ANALYSES taught and dated: primary (JCO 2019, PMID 31609651 matched - ORR 45.3%) and FINAL (Blood 2023, PMID 37130017 matched): ORR 41.5% (CR 20.8%), median DOR not reached, NO complete responder progressed; median PFS 4.3 months, 4-yr PFS 33.0%, 4-yr OS 45.3% - THE TAIL-SHAPED TRUTH. Accelerated approval 2018-06 (secondhand); CONFIRMATORY-CONVERSION STATUS UNRESOLVED this sweep - FLAGGED as the open regulatory question | PMID 37130017 + abstract read firsthand 2026-08-26

CheckMate 436 (nivolumab + brentuximab vedotin, R/R PMBCL) - READ OUT: ORR ~70-73%, CR ~37-50% (JCO 2019); 3-yr follow-up durable (Blood Adv 2023) - the chemo-free combination legacy and CAR-T bridge (secondhand citations this sweep; PACIFIC is its frontline descendant)

ZUMA-1 (NEJM 2017, PMID 29226797 matched: ORR 82%, CR 52% - eligibility INCLUDED PMBCL, snippet-confirmed) + FDA approval summary (PMID 30413526 matched: approval 2017-10-18, label includes PMBCL after >= 2 lines) + 5-yr follow-up (36821768 matched: median OS 25.8 mo, 5-yr OS 42.6% - all-LBCL figures, flagged as such for PMBCL use) + US real-world PMBCL (34474474 matched, numbers memory-grade) | PMID 29226797 + abstract read firsthand 2026-08-26

CART-SIE (Italy, Leukemia 2024): 'Axicabtagene ciloleucel treatment is more effective in primary mediastinal large B-cell lymphomas than in diffuse large B-cell lymphomas' - THE PMBCL-BETTER SIGNAL; PMID UNMATCHED (found via PMC listing only) - FLAGGED, title/venue verified

Kuruvilla et al. (Leuk Lymphoma 2008, PMID 18604722, pubmed-url-match): THE WORSE-THAN-ANALOG RECEIPT - chemo-salvage ORR 25% (PMBCL) vs 48% (DLBCL), p=0.01; 2-yr post-relapse OS 15% vs 34%, p=0.018; post-ASCT comparable IF chemosensitive (2-yr OS 67% vs 53%, NS) - the receipt that rewrote the R/R sequence. Modern post-DA-EPOCH-R R/R outcomes (41163564, matched, 2025) + ASCT-era-modern (37607645) + BV+nivo bridging (40963380) matched | PMID 18604722 + abstract read firsthand 2026-08-26

Mediastinal gray-zone lymphoma - the true between-entity: original description (Traverse-Glehen, PMID 16224207 matched); NCI prospective study (PMID 25024303 matched: n=24 DA-EPOCH-R, EFS ~62% at memory grade - WORSE than PMBCL, the reroute honesty); both 2022 classifications retain it (restricted to mediastinal EBV-negative); PD-L1/L2 pattern (29377256 matched). No open dedicated trial (the NIH pembro basket NCT03255018 is active-not-recruiting) - THE THINNESS SAID | PMID 25024303 + abstract read firsthand 2026-08-26

THE INCLUSION/EXCLUSION PATTERN with receipts (secondhand, dated): FRONTLINE OUT - POLARIX excluded 'primary mediastinal (thymic) LBCL' by name (NEJM 2022 eligibility); SKYGLO (NCT06047080) excludes BOTH PMBCL and gray-zone by name. RELAPSE IN - EPCORE NHL-1 named PMBCL eligible (JCO 2023); glofitamab NCT03533283 included it; TRANSCEND (liso-cel) included it (label basis). The pattern is why the dedicated trials exist; real-world pola-R-CHP-in-PMBCL series now filling the frontline gap (Ann Hematol 2026, secondhand)

El-Jawahri A, LeBlanc T, VanDusen H, et al. Effect of Inpatient Palliative Care on Quality of Life 2 Weeks After Hematopoietic Stem Cell Transplantation: A Randomized Clinical Trial. JAMA 2016;316(20):2094-2103 (PMID 27893130, NCT02207322) — abstract read firsthand 2026-09-10. POPULATION CAUTION, added at that read because the previous label named no population at all: this is a SINGLE-INSTITUTION randomized trial of 160 adults with HAEMATOLOGICAL malignancy hospitalized for autologous or allogeneic stem-cell transplantation, and its outcomes are quality of life, depression, anxiety, fatigue and symptom burden — it reports no survival and no adverse-event table. It is the factory's standing anchor for the PRINCIPLE that palliative care runs alongside active treatment rather than after it; it is not evidence in this tumour type and is not the source of any number on this card.

STATUS CONFLICT (the sweep's loudest): open per many US site pages (MSK/DFCI/St. Jude/Roswell/Emory), one aggregator not-recruiting, a 2021 temporary closure documented-then-reopened - registry status UNCONFIRMED, re-check MANDATORY - web-verified 2026-08-19
